file.description: An exact root-relative name from ssh_logs_list. Only explicitly allowed files can be read.

offset.description: Legacy single-file forward byte offset. Prefer nextCursor for continuation with snapshot checks. A nonzero offset cannot be combined with tail, cursor or a line range.

startLine.description: First physical line to inspect, numbered from 1 and inclusive. Defaults to 1 when only endLine is supplied. Cannot be combined with tail or a nonzero byte offset.

endLine.description: Last physical line to inspect, inclusive and not before startLine. Omit to read onward from startLine. maxLines still limits the matching records returned per page.

tail.description: Read backwards to collect the last maxLines matching records. Continue towards older records with nextCursor. This is a snapshot, not a live subscription.

maxLines.description: Maximum matching physical lines in this page, further bounded by policy and response size.

from.description: Inclusive event timestamp, not file modification time: ISO-8601 with offset (2026-10-28T10:00:00+01:00), -15m, -1h, or now-2d. If supplied without to, to is now.

to.description: Exclusive event timestamp in ISO-8601 or relative form. With only to, from is the maximum allowed range before to. Omit both to disable time filtering. Lines with missing/invalid timestamps are excluded when filtering by time. Diagnostic counts may be unknown when server-side filtering is used.

levels.description: Optional levels, for example ["ERROR","WARN"]. Common aliases are normalized. Records with no recognized level do not match an explicit level filter.

scanBytes.description: Advanced optional source-work limit, independent of response size and SSH transfer volume. Omit for normal queries: GateRook chooses server-side commands and scans up to 64 MiB per call. Do not set 1 MiB merely to request a small answer; use maxLines. A capped scan returns scanComplete=false and nextCursor.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the preceding response. Repeat the same connection, file(s), line range, filters, tail and limits. Relative time bounds stay anchored to the first call. Rotation, truncation or detected changes to the scanned snapshot invalidate the cursor; appends beyond the snapshot do not extend it.
